note: Authored blind: written by reading the source PDFs directly, before running any query, so no question was tuned to what retrieval returns. Gold labels are (source_file, page) rather than chunk ids so they survive a re-chunk. `expected` lists the acceptable LOCATIONS of one intended answer, not several distinct answers. Independent of evals/CS240.json — no question was ported, because the point of a second course is an independent read on the same retriever.
corpus: 670 chunks over 34 documents: 22 lecture decks, 5 assignment specs (A3Q1-Q2, A4Q1-Q3), 2 project specs (ArcaneMarket, RuneVault), 4 sample finals and 1 sample midterm. Excluded as not course-issued: cs247_midterm_cheatsheet.pdf (personal notes) and an unofficial grade report that matches 'CS 247' only because it lists enrolled courses.
design: CS247 is software design and C++, so the question mix probes shapes CS240 could not. Four groups: e* exact-token/identifier, p* paraphrase-cluster, c* cross-document (a pattern defined in a lecture and also the whole subject of an assignment), s* straightforward. The p* group is the deliberate stress case: six separate decks each carry a slide beginning literally 'Design Principle:', so surface form alone cannot pick the right one.

queries.query: What does the CompositeIterator class do?
queries.note: EXACT-TOKEN (code-embedded). 'A tree-walking iterator that flattens a Composite'. The identifier appears only inside a code listing, where surrounding text is syntax rather than explanation — the case CS240's corpus had no analogue for.

queries.query: In the Weather-O-Rama example, what are the three display elements?
queries.note: EXACT-TOKEN (prose). Current conditions, statistics, and forecast displays. 'Weather-O-Rama' is a rare literal in running prose — the same shape as CS240's 'Leo', which ranked 1.

queries.query: What is the Starbuzz Coffee example used to illustrate?
queries.note: EXACT-TOKEN (prose). The Decorator pattern's running example.

queries.query: What does the Gumball Machine example demonstrate?
queries.note: EXACT-TOKEN (prose). The State pattern's running example.

queries.query: What is CRTP, the Curiously Recurring Template Pattern, mentioned in relation to?
queries.note: EXACT-TOKEN (acronym). Raised as an alternative to virtual functions for polymorphic behaviour in Decorator.

queries.query: In ArcaneMarket, how much do the four Forges cost?
queries.note: EXACT-TOKEN (invented domain vocabulary). Ironhold, Bronzeworks, Coppergate and Steelspire, 200 Reagents each.

queries.query: In RuneVault, what is the Cipher Gem?
queries.note: EXACT-TOKEN (invented domain vocabulary). One of the two major items.

queries.query: Which design principle says to favour composition over inheritance?
queries.note: PARAPHRASE-CLUSTER. One of six 'Design Principle:' slides spread across six decks, all structurally identical in their opening.

queries.query: Which design principle says classes should be open for extension but closed for modification?
queries.note: PARAPHRASE-CLUSTER. Competes with the other five 'Design Principle:' slides.

queries.query: Which design principle says to depend upon abstractions and not upon concrete classes?
queries.note: PARAPHRASE-CLUSTER. Competes with the other five 'Design Principle:' slides.

queries.query: Which design principle says to strive for loosely coupled designs between objects that interact?
queries.note: PARAPHRASE-CLUSTER. Competes with the other five 'Design Principle:' slides.

queries.query: What are the real-world use cases given for the Observer pattern?
queries.note: PARAPHRASE-CLUSTER. Nearly every pattern deck carries a 'Real World Use Cases' slide, so the section heading is uninformative and only the content disambiguates.

queries.query: What is the difference between aggregation and composition in UML?
queries.note: PARAPHRASE-CLUSTER. Two adjacent near-twin slides, each defining a 'part-of' relation; the answer needs both.

queries.query: What problem does the Decorator pattern solve?
queries.note: CROSS-DOCUMENT (m5/m6 shape). The lecture DEFINES it; A3Q1_Spec.pdf is nine chunks entirely about implementing Decorator. On CS240 the assignment won this shape of contest.

queries.query: What relationship does the Observer pattern define between objects?
queries.note: CROSS-DOCUMENT. 'A one-to-many relationship between objects'. Competes with A3Q2_Spec.pdf and the Observer question on the sample finals.

queries.query: What does the Iterator pattern provide?
queries.note: CROSS-DOCUMENT. 'Access the elements of an aggregate object sequentially without exposing its underlying representation.' Competes with A4Q1_Spec.pdf.

queries.query: Which patterns make up the MVC compound pattern?
queries.note: CROSS-DOCUMENT. Observer, Strategy and Composite. Competes with A4Q3_Spec.pdf, which is an MVC implementation task.

queries.query: What does the Composite pattern let you build?
queries.note: CROSS-DOCUMENT. Tree structures of both individual objects and compositions. Competes with A4Q1_Spec.pdf's menu-composite task.

queries.query: What iterator traits must the assignment's iterators define to work with STL algorithms?
queries.note: CROSS-DOCUMENT, REVERSED. Here the ASSIGNMENT is the correct answer ('Tip — STL Iterator Traits'), competing against lecture decks 8 and 16. Pairs with c3 to test whether the lecture/assignment bias runs in one direction or both.

queries.query: What is the difference between an entity object and a value object?
queries.note: Entity objects have distinct identity; value objects with equal attributes are identical.

queries.query: What is the PImpl idiom and why is it used?
queries.note: Pointer to Implementation: forward-declare a nested Impl struct to hide the representation.

queries.query: What are the special member functions that the C++ compiler generates by default?
queries.note: p3 introduces them, p34 summarises 'six of them; if one needs to be hand-crafted, likely all do'.

queries.query: What is the difference between a shallow copy and a deep copy?
queries.note: Two adjacent slides, one per side of the distinction.

queries.query: What is the copy-swap idiom?
queries.note: Assignment via constructing a copy and swapping, so the operator is exception-safe.

queries.query: What is the difference between an lvalue and an rvalue?
queries.note: 'An lvalue is anything with an address'.

queries.query: What does the requires clause mean in a CS 247 interface specification?
queries.note: Preconditions: constraints that must hold before the method is called.

queries.query: What is a UML sequence diagram?
queries.note: A graphical model of communication events between objects over time.

queries.query: What do multiplicity annotations constrain in a UML association?
queries.note: The number of allowable links in an association.
